context: The inputs are the traversals preorder = [3, 9, 2, 1, 7] and inorder = [9, 3, 1, 2, 7], with distinct node values.
The reconstructed tree has root 3, left child 9, and right child 2. Node 2 has left child 1 and right child 7. Nodes 9, 1, and 7 are leaves.
description: Beside each of the five nodes is a pair of full-length preorder and inorder arrays. Only the segments for the current subproblem are colored. Unrelated positions are light gray. In each subproblem, teal marks its root, blue its left subtree, and purple its right subtree.

Light gray cells still belong to the original array but lie outside the current subproblem. At a leaf, the active sequence contains only the root, with both subtree segments empty. The table identifies the root and both segments of each active sequence. Its left and right subtree roots are read from the parent–child edges.

frames.explanation: A node value can have different colors in different subproblems. For example, 2 lies in the purple right-subtree segment of the top-level arrays for root 3. In the arrays for the subtree rooted at 2, it is the teal root element. All five circular nodes in the tree itself are green.
frames.title: How each subproblem splits preorder and inorder

result: Each subproblem follows the same rule: preorder identifies the root, and inorder separates the left and right ranges. Empty intervals on either side of a leaf return null references.
summary: Root 3 splits off left leaf 9 and a right subtree rooted at 2. Node 2 splits off left leaf 1 and right leaf 7. Each node is labeled with its active traversal ranges.
